_comment: Protected-unless-improving manifest for the self-learning harness. The harness-optimize skill loads this and SKIPS protected components. The only allowed change to a protected component is a verified net improvement: build a strictly-better replacement, confirm harness-check still passes, update this manifest, THEN retire the old one, logged in CHANGELOG.md. A protected component that seems obsolete is surfaced to the owner, never silently removed.

protected_hooks.removal_rule: Never remove. Single source of truth for WHERE harness state and transcripts live. Any script needing a state path imports it; a second derivation is how a reader ends up in an empty directory reporting '0 corrections'.
Never remove. The raw capture layer everything downstream reads. An unregistered capture hook silently kills the whole loop.
Only if memory-seeding moves into a strictly-better mechanism.
Never remove. Without it the self-tuning loop is blind.
Never remove. The drift sensor that makes silent failure loud, and the only ritual scheduler (cadence nudges at session start).
Report-only use-rate ranking for the pruning pass. Removable if pruning candidates are measured some strictly-better way.
Cost signal for pruning. Removable only if spend is measured elsewhere.
Never remove. Destructive-command and push-to-main safety.
Without it .agents/rules/*.md never load at edit time. Remove only if the rules move into always-on AGENTS.md context.
The explicit are-you-sure before a migration, workflow, build-config, lock or .env edit. Remove only if those edits get a strictly-better confirmation path.
Surfaces long-tail memory notes. Before sunsetting, check reflect has not demoted index lines on the assumption recall surfaces them.

protected_skills.removal_rule: The PR review-and-fix loop; the gate before main. Never remove without a strictly-better replacement.

Drives a PR from opened to merged across pushes, CI runs and review threads (land.py picks the next step). Without it nobody watches CI after a push or answers threads. Replace only with a loop that keeps the same order and never-rules.
The self-driving loop: what the owner asks when they don't know what to ask. Its signals.py also feeds the SessionStart next-action line. Replace only with something that ranks the same signals.
The product-analytics feedback loop into the backlog. Removable only if funnel drop-offs reach the backlog some strictly-better way.
Keeps the setup-time market check (docs/product/VALIDATION.md) current. Monthly by design; low use is expected, not dormancy.
Release checklist (store requirements, OTA safety). Low use between releases is expected, not dormancy.
Walks the incident runbook and proposes the rollback before any diagnosis. Rarely used by design (incidents are rare); low use is never a pruning signal.
Sets up scheduled rituals with consent. Used once or twice per project; never a pruning candidate for low use.

protected_agents.removal_rule: The correctness/security reviewer the pr-review loop depends on.
The final ruling on irreversible calls (model: fable). pr-review step 4b and the pr-review workflow depend on it. A model downgrade is a change to propose, never an automatic prune.
Cheap sweeps (model: haiku) for next, dependency triage and CI logs. Removable if those sweeps move somewhere cheaper.

workflows._comment: Claude Code Workflow scripts (opt-in, token-heavy). The SKILL.md of the same name is the default route and the only one in Codex, so a workflow is an accelerator, never the sole path. Keep each in step with its skill.

evals._comment: Skill evals in claude plugin eval format (.agents is packaged as a plugin via .agents/.claude-plugin/plugin.json). harness-optimize reads result deltas from .agents/evals/results/. Every skill edit that changes behaviour should keep or raise its case scores.

data_files.removal_rule: Git-tracked memory. Never auto-pruned; consolidation happens only via the reflect skill.
Prune an individual rule only if it is verifiably obsolete.

transcripts._comment: Where the extractor, spend ledger and healthcheck READ session transcripts. Claude Code: <claude_projects_dir>/<slugified repo path>[--claude-worktrees-<id>]/*.jsonl. Codex: rollout JSONL files matched by codex_sessions_glob, kept only when their session_meta cwd is this repo (or a worktree of it); parsing is best-effort (user messages + tool names) and unknown records are skipped. Set codex=false to ignore Codex entirely. Env overrides: APPBOX_CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR, APPBOX_CODEX_SESSIONS_GLOB. Capture/state live in $APPBOX_STATE_DIR or ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/appbox/<slug>/, never in the repo.

owner_asks._comment: Skills and subagent roles that reach product-judgement calls (.agents/rules/product-judgement.md). tests/harness/test_owner_asks.py fails if a listed skill loses its '## Ask the owner' step or a listed role stops returning ⚖️ QUESTION blocks. Removing an entry is a harness change: say why in the PR.

complexity_budget._comment: An ACCRETION ALARM, not a dismantle mandate. Over budget means harness-optimize owes a deliberate look for something to retire, never an automatic removal. Protected components are exempt and memory is never auto-pruned. Limits sit above the template baseline so they fire on growth; raising one is fine when it is deliberate and logged in CHANGELOG.md.

spend_budget._comment: SOFT weekly spend budget in input-token equivalents (see spend_ledger.py). null = off. Set it from a measured baseline: `python3 .claude/hooks/spend_ledger.py --days 28 --by day`, then ~1.5x a typical week. Over budget is a SessionStart nudge; nothing is blocked.

sunset._comment: Removal is staged, never abrupt. Non-protected components only.
protocol: 1. Capability re-test: in a clean session WITHOUT the component, give the task that motivated it and check the agent gets it right 3/3. Scaffolding the model has outgrown is drag; scaffolding still doing work is not.
2. Move (don't delete) to .claude/_sunset/ and log the date + the 3/3 evidence in CHANGELOG.md.
3. Wait two weeks of real use. No regression -> delete. Regression -> restore and annotate 'still load-bearing as of <date>'.
4. A hook must also be unregistered from .claude/settings.json (and the Codex adapter regenerated) in step 2, or it keeps firing.

cadence._comment: Days after which the SessionStart healthcheck nudges (then escalates at 2x and 3x) to run each ritual. Last-run stamps live in state.json, written by `python3 .claude/hooks/harness_paths.py stamp <ritual>` at the end of each ritual. `scheduled` lists rituals a Routine or cron already runs (set by the routines skill); they're never nudged. Dependency PRs reach the next skill through GitHub signals, not a cadence.

registered_hook_check._comment: Hooks that MUST appear in .claude/settings.json (and so in the generated .codex/hooks.json). Wired, not just present on disk.
